\section{Canonical equations}
\label{sec:equations}

The equation identities below are canonical SCI-ALIGN v0.1 author-draft
identifiers.  Parenthetical aliases preserve the recovered independent-core
identities A1--A19.  Equations are conditional on the identities, producer
semantics, operator registry, and availability rules in
Sections~\ref{sec:definitions}--\ref{sec:assumptions}.

\subsection{Clock normalization, grid, and assignment}

Checked native time on detector-reference coordinate is
\begin{equation}
 t_{ik}^{\rm ref}=(E_i-E_{i_{\rm ref}})_{\rm sec}+u_{ik}
 +\delta_{i\rightarrow\rm ref},
 \qquad i_{\rm ref}=D,\quad \delta_{{\rm ref}\rightarrow{\rm ref}}=0.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-001}\label{eq:clock}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves recovered-core identity A1.  A positive offset is
added, acquisition bounds use the same transform, and the operation occurs
exactly once before ordering, assignment, gap, interval, or interpolation
logic.

For detector phase \(\phi_D\), cadence \(h_D>0\), and mapped acquisition
bounds, the nominal lattice is
\begin{align}
 t_s&=\phi_D+s h_D,\notag\\
 s_{\min}&=\left\lceil\frac{B_D^- -\phi_D}{h_D}\right\rceil,
 &s_{\max}&=\left\lceil\frac{B_D^+ -\phi_D}{h_D}\right\rceil-1,
 &\mathcal S&=\{s_{\min},\ldots,s_{\max}\}.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-002}\label{eq:grid}
\end{align}
\noindent This preserves A2.  The stable ALIGN slot identity is \((o,s)\).
Within a selected materialized view, \(j\) is a derived local storage row;
it is never external identity and cannot be used to reconstruct \(s\) without
the explicit view relation.  Empty \(\mathcal S\) is an unsuccessful ALIGN
operation.  Symbol \(n\) is reserved for stable RTC output-sample identity.

An original detector row uses explicit round-half-up assignment:
\begin{equation}
 s(k)=\left\lfloor
 \frac{t_{Dk}^{\rm ref}-\phi_D}{h_D}+\frac12
 \right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 \left|t_{Dk}^{\rm ref}-t_{s(k)}\right|
 \leq\epsilon_{\rm slot}<\frac{h_D}{2}.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-003}\label{eq:slot}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A3.  The corrected native time and residual
\(t_{Dk}^{\rm ref}-t_{s(k)}\) remain distinct from nominal slot time.  Collisions,
ambiguity, duplicate/nonmonotonic coordinates, or rows outside declared
support fail closed.

\subsection{Field operators and paired detector mapping}

For a continuous scalar at common time \(t_s\), bounded adjacent
interpolation inside one valid run is
\begin{align}
 \lambda_s&=\frac{t_s-t_a}{t_b-t_a},\qquad 0<\lambda_s<1,\notag\\
 y_s&=(1-\lambda_s)v_a+\lambda_s v_b.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-004}\label{eq:linear}
\end{align}
\noindent This preserves A4.  Exact coincidence is one-hot original support;
no extrapolation or skipping across invalid rows is allowed.

For a circular field of declared period \(P\), using signed shortest
difference \(d_P(a,b)\in[-P/2,P/2)\),
\begin{equation}
 y_s=\operatorname{wrap}_P\!\left(v_a+\lambda_s d_P(v_a,v_b)\right).
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-005}\label{eq:circular}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A5.  Exactly antipodal inputs are unavailable unless
an explicit unwrap authority resolves the interpolation path; the endpoint
choice in the half-open difference interval is not such authority.

The canonical paired detector-coordinate invariant is
\begin{equation}
 x^A=A_{\rm ALIGN}x^{\rm acq},
 \qquad
 r^A=A_{\rm ALIGN}r^{\rm acq}.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-006}\label{eq:paired}
\end{equation}
The two applications have the same native occurrences, weights, residuals,
slots, source-relation identity, and origin/synthesis state, while numerical
validity and payload availability remain coordinate-specific.  Equation
\ref{eq:paired} does not authorize a mapping across a Tune or mapping-revision
boundary.

For one fixed realized mapping and processing window \(q\), a block view is
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol y_q=
 \begin{bmatrix}
 S_qG_D&0&0\\
 0&S_qI_T&0\\
 0&0&S_qI_H
 \end{bmatrix}
 \begin{bmatrix}
 \boldsymbol v_D\\ \boldsymbol v_T\\ \boldsymbol v_H
 \end{bmatrix}
 \equiv A_q\boldsymbol v .
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-007}\label{eq:block}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A6.  \(G_D\) includes the invariant in
Equation~\ref{eq:paired}; absent HWPR is typed unavailable, not zero.  Circular
mapping is the corresponding nonlinear map and Equation~\ref{eq:block} its
local linearization away from ambiguity.

\subsection{Conditional continuity surrogate and windows}

If and only if a signal-domain authority closes \code{SCI-ALIGN-ODQ-104}, an
authorized internal linear-gap surrogate for \(g\) absent slots between valid
endpoint values \(z_0,z_{g+1}\) may take the form
\begin{equation}
 \widehat z_\ell=\left(1-\frac{\ell}{g+1}\right)z_0
 +\frac{\ell}{g+1}z_{g+1},
 \qquad \ell=1,\ldots,g.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-008}\label{eq:gap}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A7 as conditional reasoning, not authorization.
Every realized cell retains both endpoint identities and weights, synthesized
origin, zero acquired exposure, and conditional response.  Leading/trailing,
over-limit, invalid-endpoint, or cross-revision gaps are unavailable; no long
gap is partially filled.

When a separately requested fixed-duration \emph{processing-window} policy of
duration \(L>0\) is admitted, it may resolve to
\begin{equation}
 M=\left\lfloor\frac{L}{h_D}+\frac12\right\rfloor\geq1,
 \qquad
 \mathcal S_q=[s_{\min}+qM,\min\{s_{\min}+(q+1)M,s_{\min}+N\}),
 \quad q=0,\ldots,\left\lceil\frac NM\right\rceil-1.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-009}\label{eq:windows}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A8 only for the stated conditional construction.  It
does not define, replace, or renumber producer-authoritative physical scans.
Final partial and short windows retain identity.

The corresponding selector is
\begin{equation}
 (S_q)_{as}=\mathbf 1\{s=s_{\min}+qM+a\},\qquad s\in\mathcal S_q.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-010}\label{eq:selection}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A9.  Slicing changes support and window response but
not units, slot identity, physical-scan identity, or origin.

\subsection{Response and uncertainty}

For fixed \(A_q\) and temporal template \(\boldsymbol p\), the conditional
response is
\begin{equation}
 R_q(\boldsymbol p)=
 \frac{\partial\E[\boldsymbol y_q\mid A_q]}{\partial\alpha}
 =A_q\boldsymbol p,
 \qquad
 \E[\boldsymbol v]=\alpha\boldsymbol p+\boldsymbol\mu_0.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-011}\label{eq:response}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A10.  It is conditional ALIGN response, not a
downstream estimator response.

For uniform samples and fractional target \((k+\alpha)h\),
\(0\leq\alpha\leq1\), linear interpolation relative to an ideal fractional
delay has response
\begin{equation}
 H_\alpha(\omega)=e^{-i\omega\alpha h}
 \left[(1-\alpha)+\alpha e^{i\omega h}\right].
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-012}\label{eq:fractional-response}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A11.  \(H_\alpha(0)=1\); amplitude and phase are not
unity in general.  Gap response is row-specific and nonstationary.

For fixed affine mapping and supplied full joint native covariance,
\begin{align}
 \E[\boldsymbol y_q\mid A_q]&=A_q\E[\boldsymbol v\mid A_q],\notag\\
 C_{y_q\mid A_q}&=A_qC_{v\mid A_q}A_q^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-013}\label{eq:covariance}
\end{align}
\noindent This preserves A12, including known cross-time, cross-detector, and
cross-stream terms.

For Equation~\ref{eq:linear}, one scalar variance is
\begin{equation}
 \Var(y_s)=(1-\lambda_s)^2\Var(v_a)+\lambda_s^2\Var(v_b)
 +2\lambda_s(1-\lambda_s)\Cov(v_a,v_b).
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-014}\label{eq:linear-variance}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A13.  Shared endpoints induce output covariance;
smoother appearance or smaller diagonal variance is not new information.

For differentiable signals and timing parameter vector
\(\boldsymbol\eta\), the first-order timing term is
\begin{equation}
 C_{\rm timing}=J_\eta C_\eta J_\eta^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad (J_\eta)_{ab}=\frac{\partial y_a}{\partial\eta_b}.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-015}\label{eq:timing-covariance}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A14.  It is systematic/response uncertainty, not
detector noise.

The full reporting target is
\begin{equation}
 C_y=C_{y\mid A}+C_{\rm timing}+C_{\rm interp.model}
 +C_{\rm policy/selection}.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-016}\label{eq:full-uncertainty}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A15.  Missing terms are unavailable, not zero;
conditional claims name what was conditioned upon.

For twice differentiable scalar truth on a bracket of width
\(\Delta=t_b-t_a\),
\begin{equation}
 |f(t)-If(t)|\leq\frac{\Delta^2}{8}
 \sup_{s\in[t_a,t_b]}|f''(s)|.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-017}\label{eq:interp-bound}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A16 and is available only with a scientifically
justified curvature bound.

\subsection{Exposure and local state}

For nominal cell \(I_s\) and detector occurrence or stable detector identity
\(d\), physical acquired exposure and its valid-original subset are
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 e^{\rm acq}_{sd}&=\begin{cases}
 |I_s\cap I^{\rm native}_{kd}|,
   &\text{one original physical detector occurrence }k,\\
 0,&\text{synthesized, missing, or unoccupied support,}
 \end{cases}\\[2pt]
 e^{\rm vo}_{sd}&=e^{\rm acq}_{sd}
 \mathbf 1\{\text{original payload and required ALIGN-local mapping facts valid}\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-018}\label{eq:exposure}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A17 while separating physical acquisition from
scientific usability.  An original-invalid payload may have
\(e^{\rm acq}_{sd}>0\) and \(e^{\rm vo}_{sd}=0\).  Synthesized/surrogate and
missing/unoccupied support add no acquired exposure.  Nominal duration,
elapsed span, guarded/retained/use-qualified exposure, and downstream weight
remain separate later facts and never rewrite physical acquisition.

Each output cell has the product state
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal S_{\rm ALIGN}=(\text{origin},\text{local validity},\text{method},\text{reason},
 \text{source IDs},\text{weights}).
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-019}\label{eq:quality}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves A18, specialized so that local validity is not AST
validity or downstream eligibility.

For a factual ALIGN-local relation requiring an original valid detector value
and aligned field set \(\mathcal V\),
\begin{equation}
 m_{sd}^{\rm local}=
 \mathbf 1\{D_{sd}\text{ is original and locally valid}\}
 \prod_{v\in\mathcal V}
 \mathbf 1\{T_{vs}\text{ is available and locally valid}\}.
 \tag{SCI-ALIGN-EQ-020}\label{eq:local-support}
\end{equation}
\noindent This preserves recovered-core A19 only as an ALIGN-local
mapping/support fact.  It is not a universal eligibility bit, AST validity,
or authorization for an estimator.  A named-use owner supplies any additional
predicate, and its designated evaluator applies every applicable restriction.
